chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Ali ibn Saeed, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who hired a donkey, then turned with it to the owners of the clothes (shop), and bought from them a garment or two garments, and left the donkey. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The donkey is returned to its owner, and the one who took the two garments is pursued, and there is no cutting upon him; rather, it is betrayal (of trust).'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a hired animal is left at a shop while the buyer purchases goods?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between *qat'* (the specific corporal punishment for theft) and *khiyanah* (breach of trust), ruling that the shopkeeper’s retention of the clothes constitutes the latter. This distinction is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that not all unauthorized retention of property qualifies as *sariqah* (theft) requiring amputation, but rather depends on the nature of the possession and the intent. The ruling underscores the importance of fulfilling contractual obligations and the moral weight of trust (*amanah*) in commercial transactions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Ali Bin Saeed who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who hired a donkey. Then he went to the owners of the clothes (shop), so he bought a cloth or two clothes from them, and left the donkey (with them). So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The donkey would be returned to its owner, and the one who went away with the two clothes would be followed, and there is no cutting upon him, but rather, it is betrayal (of trust)’.
